questions.stem: A metallic rod of length $l$ is rotated with a frequency $f$ about one of its ends perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field $B$. The induced emf between the ends of the rod is:
questions.solution:
The induced emf is given by $e = \frac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$.
Since $\omega = 2\pi f$, we have:
$e = \frac{1}{2} B (2\pi f) l^2 = \pi f B l^2$.

questions.stem: A conducting rod of length $l$ is rotated with a constant angular speed $\omega$ about one of its ends in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field $B$. The induced EMF between the two ends of the rod is:
questions.solution: The induced EMF is given by $e = \int_0^l v B dr = \int_0^l (\omega r) B dr = B \omega \left[\frac{r^2}{2}\right]_0^l = \frac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$.

questions.stem: A conducting rod of length $1\ \mathrm{m}$ is rotated with a constant angular speed of $4\ \mathrm{rad/s}$ about an axis passing through one of its ends and perpendicular to its length. A uniform magnetic field of $2\ \mathrm{T}$ exists parallel to the axis of rotation. The induced emf between the two ends of the rod is ______ $\mathrm{V}$.
questions.solution:
The induced emf in a rotating rod is given by $e = \frac{1}{2} B \omega L^2$.
Given $B = 2\ \mathrm{T}$, $\omega = 4\ \mathrm{rad/s}$, and $L = 1\ \mathrm{m}$.
$e = \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 4 \times 1^2 = 4\ \mathrm{V}$.

questions.stem: A conducting rod of length $l$ is rotated with a constant angular velocity $\omega$ about one of its ends in a plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field $B$. The induced electromotive force between the ends of the rod is:
questions.solution:
The induced emf in a rotating rod of length $l$ about one end is:
$e = \int_0^l v B \, \mathrm{d}r = \int_0^l (\omega r) B \, \mathrm{d}r = B \omega \left[ \frac{r^2}{2} \right]_0^l = \frac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$.

questions.stem: A metallic rod of length $l$ is rotated with a constant angular speed $\omega$ about an axis passing through one end and perpendicular to its length, in a uniform magnetic field $B$ parallel to the axis of rotation. The induced emf between the ends of the rod is:
questions.solution:
The induced emf is given by integrating $de = B v dr = B (\omega r) dr$ from $0$ to $l$.
$e = B \omega \int_{0}^{l} r dr = \frac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$.

questions.stem: A metallic rod of length $1 \mathrm{m}$ is rotated with a frequency of $10 \mathrm{Hz}$ about an axis passing through its one end and perpendicular to its length, in a uniform magnetic field of $0.1 \mathrm{T}$ directed perpendicular to the plane of rotation. The induced emf between the ends of the rod is $\frac{\pi}{x} \mathrm{V}$. The value of $x$ is:
questions.solution:
The induced emf in a rotating rod is given by $\varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} B \omega L^2$.
Here, $L = 1 \mathrm{m}$, $B = 0.1 \mathrm{T}$, and $f = 10 \mathrm{Hz} \implies \omega = 2\pi f = 20\pi \mathrm{rad/s}$.
$\varepsilon = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.1 \times 20\pi \times 1^2 = \pi \mathrm{V}$.
Comparing with $\frac{\pi}{x}$, we get $x = 1$.
